correctness.rationale: An interior point gives positive support distance p=q−d cosθ in every direction, so M+p uθ is an embedded regular analytic polar curve. Its tangent has one full turn because its argument equals θ plus the argument of p′+ip with p>0. Thus the curvature numerator N=p²+2p′²−pp″ is everywhere nonnegative exactly when the bounded region is convex. For h=q/a, e=1−b²/a², x=cosθ/h and z=d/a, use h²+(h′)²=1−e+ex², h cosθ−h′ sinθ=x and h+h″=(1−e)/h³ to obtain the frozen cubic for N/a². The minor-axis reflection permits z≥0. The minimum is on x∈[0,1]; 2ex/(1+ex²) is strictly increasing, so in the interior-minimum regime substitution gives sign ex²−2e+1, whereas at x=1 the minimum is (1−z)(1+e−2z). The join 2e/(1+e) lies strictly below (1+e)/2 and, for e>1/2, above the lower threshold. These tests give exactly the closed window and the stated curvature-zero cases. Analyticity excludes boundary segments; outside the window the minimum is negative. The focal pedal satisfies |M+p uθ|²=a², with z=√e strictly between the thresholds. Expanding √((1−2τ)/(1−τ)) at τ=b²/a² verifies the width coefficient 5/8.

value.rationale: The major axis is geometrically canonical and includes both the center and the foci. A complete convexity test there is more than interpolation between two classical examples: sufficiently eccentric ellipses have a nonconvex center pedal, then a convex band, then another nonconvex regime before the boundary. The sharp interval and its fourth-order width give a useful exact shape criterion where an approximate rule based on focal distance can fail.
residual_risks: Value is the complete natural axial classification, not a claim about general conics or off-axis pedals.
